sources.title: My original-fence and bounded CPU execution
Exact two-head toy arithmetic and fixed-width count
sources.details: For query1 over keys0,1, head0=(3/4)[10,0,0,0]+(1/4)[0,20,0,0]=[7.5,5,0,0]; head1=(1/4)[4,8,0,0]+(3/4)[12,0,0,0]=[10,2,0,0]. Ordered concat gives [7.5,5,0,0,10,2,0,0]. Each head's ratios sum to1 over allowed keys. Fixed width8 divided by heads2/4 gives head_dim4/2; 8%3!=0. Default four biasless 8x8 projection weights yield 256 parameters for either 2 or4 heads (extra implementation cross-check, not a new claimed course result).

claims.statement: Each head has its own learned Q/K/V projections, computes scaled causal attention over all allowed positions, then heads concatenate and use a learned output projection. Distinct heads allow different readings; the architecture assigns no fixed grammar/object roles.
claims.scope: Standard MHA default path kv_heads=heads; feature subspaces may differ. No guaranteed learned semantics or actual parallel wall-clock scheduling is asserted.

evidence.locator: §3.2.1 Eq.(1); §3.2.2 head_i and MultiHead formulas; §3.2.3 decoder bullet
evidence.supports: Defines scaled attention, learned per-head projections, concatenation/output projection, and each decoder position's complete permitted prefix. Projection matrices contain no preset semantic labels.
Confirms the actual default implementation applies those projections, masks, head split and output map; positions are not split across heads.

claims.statement: The specified head0/head1 ratios yield [7.5,5,0,0] and [10,2,0,0], ordered concat [7.5,5,0,0,10,2,0,0], then an 8→8 output Linear retains width at this same query position.
claims.scope: Specified toy V/ratios for query1 and allowed keys0,1; it is separate from the random-input code and does not give numerical post-Linear values.

evidence.locator: Exact 3/4,1/4 weighted sums and ordered concatenation
evidence.supports: Independently recomputes every displayed feature, normalized head ratios and 2x4=8 dimensionality.
Supports weighted value sum and a width-restoring output projection.
Fraction arithmetic gives exact values; a separately constructed compatible float64 Q/K recovers those ratios through actual manual_attention.

verification.expected: Displayed toy outputs/concat exactly; weight sums1; 8 output features.
verification.observed: All exact Fraction values match; synthetic row weights [[0.75,0.25],[0.25,0.75]], max output error0.
verification.details: Ratios normalize over allowed key positions, not value-feature columns. Ratios are dimensionless; V/output numbers are toy features. No assumed output Linear weights or trained behavior.
verification.tolerance: Fraction equality exact; synthetic float64 atol=1e-12, rtol=0.

claims.statement: The unmodified width8/heads2 fence returns out [1,4,8] and K [1,2,4,4]; full feature projections [1,4,8] reshape to [1,4,2,4] then transpose to [1,2,4,4], and mixed heads concatenate back to each input position before output Linear.
claims.scope: Default one-batch four-position MHA; K axes are batch,heads,key_positions,features, whereas score axes end in key_positions.

evidence.supports: Three full feature projections, feature splitting, head-position transpose, reverse transpose/contiguous/view and same-position output Linear.
Last feature axis changes according to out_features, leading batch/position axes remain intact.
Justifies reshape versus actual axis exchange and reverse view; no positions are removed.
Confirms axes1,2 are swapped rather than redistributing sequence positions.
Actual fence sizes, independent per-head/per-query reference, projection content change and unchanged prefix after future perturbation.

verification.observed: All exact shapes match; independent max absolute output error5.960464477539063e-08; output Linear changes concat content by max0.8972471952438354. Future perturbation gives prefix error0.
verification.details: Real original fence executed through CPU helper; independent loop slices projection rows per head and for each query uses every prefix key. Score and K coincidentally share numeric4 axes but have different meanings. Float32 numeric comparisons atol1e-6, rtol1e-5.

claims.scope: This CausalAttention implementation with default kv_heads=heads; divisibility is its split-head contract.

claims.statement: The returned K/V tuple is an attention cache: earlier K/V can be reused for later token generation; its final axis is per-head features, not attention-weight candidate positions.
claims.scope: Single-layer tuple cache in this repository; no claim of full Transformers Cache API or measured generation speed.

Real tuple stores K/V before optional repeated KV heads; appends cache along sequence axis, offsets query positions and returns new_cache.
